title: ‘Dystopian’: Co-op becomes latest firm to put staff under AI surveillance
key_facts: Co-op Legal Services uses AI models to record, analyse and score calls between advisers and customers about probate, wills and estates.
A model from OpenAI assesses more than 50 aspects of each call and gives managers pass or fail scores.
A whistleblower called the system "oppressive and dystopian"; one worker said they are monitored for several hours a day.
The monitoring was introduced in the last couple of months for dozens of legal services staff and is partly used to find ways to improve sales performance.
Co-op says the AI is a support tool, not a decision-maker.
The Communication Workers Union and the International Labour Organization warned about stress and weak regulation.
quote_evidence: In a system described as “oppressive and dystopian” by a whistleblower, Co-op Legal Services is using AI models to record, analyse and award a percentage score for interactions between agents and customers seeking advice about probate, wills and estates.
The Co-op said the AI is used solely as a support tool, is not a decision-maker, and helps leaders “support colleagues and continuously improve the experience we provide to clients”.
why_it_matters_hint: AI call scoring spreads to more workplaces, with staff reporting stress and unions pushing back.
notes: Claims come from an anonymous whistleblower and a union; the Co-op disputes the characterisation.
